rootCause: Weighing metaphor was illegible (beam rendered as a short upright hairline instead of a tilted bar with weights at its ends), the counterweight used a second full-strength accent that outshone the gold, and the headline wrapped into a 5-line low-sitting stack.
changesMade: Set the large counterweight Circle to accent 'orange' at 0.5 opacity so gold is the single dominant accent and 'small gold beats large dim' hierarchy reads correctly
Rotated the beam Line to 14deg, lengthened it to 70%, and raised it to offsetY -16 so the tilt visibly dips toward the gold weight
Repositioned both weight Circles onto the beam ends: dim circle offsetX -30/offsetY -21, gold circle offsetX 30/offsetY -11 (gold side lower = it wins)
Moved the vertical fulcrum Line to offsetY -10 under the beam center so beam+fulcrum read as a balance scale
Shortened headline wrapping to a 2-line phrase 'WANT MOST / BEATS WANT NOW' (within 4-line limit) and raised the block via a scene-level placement
Shifted the gold glow to offsetY -6 to sit behind the balance rather than the text, keeping intensity 0.3 (single subordinate glow)
expectedEffect: The frame now reads instantly as a tilted balance where a small gold weight outweighs a large dim one, with gold as the only dominant accent and a clean two-line centered headline under the beam.
